home.heroMotto: For the Upliftment of Veda Gurukulas
home.heroDescription: With the boundless grace of the Jagadgurus of Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri, we are devoted to supporting Veda Gurukulas through seva, śraddhā and saṁskāra, and to sustaining the timeless Guru–Shishya Parampara.
home.vedaVidyaSubtitle: The Vedas are the foundation of Sanātana Dharma — an unbroken oral tradition spanning millennia, preserved through the sacred bond of Guru and Shishya.
home.vedaVidyaShlokaTranslation: Rooted in the four Vedas, Dharma stands eternal — nourishing life, order, and truth.
home.whyGurukulasSubtitle: Adi Shankaracharya's timeless injunction: 'Let the Veda be studied daily.'
home.whyGurukulasPara1: Inspired by the timeless injunction of Adi Shankaracharya — {shloka} ('let the Veda be studied daily') — Veda Gurukulas stand as sacred institutions that preserve the very heartbeat of Sanātana Dharma. Rooted in the venerable Guru–Śiṣya Paramparā, they are not merely centres of learning, but sanctuaries where knowledge is lived, discipline is cultivated, and saṁskāra is imbibed through constant guidance and practice.
home.whyGurukulasPara2: In an age of rapid change, they remain timeless beacons, ensuring that the wisdom of the Ṛṣis continues to illuminate generations with purity, authenticity, and unwavering continuity.
home.whyGurukulasPara3: In humble alignment with this sacred ideal, Śrī Śivasaṅkalpa Vṛnda is devoted to supporting and strengthening Veda Gurukulas. Through dedicated efforts toward the welfare of Vedic students and Adhyāpakas, the Vṛnda seeks to contribute — however modestly — to the continuity of this timeless heritage, for the benefit of society and for {lokaKalyana}.
home.gurukulasTitle: Gurukulas We Are Privileged to Serve
home.gurukulasSubtitle: We work directly with Vedic Gurukulas in Karnataka, understanding their needs and providing sustained support.

home.sringeriPara: The name 'Sri Shivasankalpa' was bestowed as a blessing by His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri. Sri Shivasankalpa Vṛnda operates with the boundless grace and divine blessings of His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam and His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam.
home.sringeriNote: The Vṛnda considers the blessings and approval of the Sringeri Jagadgurus as paramount in all its endeavours.

vedaVruksha.alt: Veda Vṛkṣa — the Veda as a banyan tree. Brahman (Īśvara) is its root; śraddhā and dharma water and nourish it, and a guru teaches his students at its foot. One trunk divides into the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda and Atharvaveda, with some of their śākhās as twigs and a small twig showing the Saṃhitā, Brāhmaṇa, Āraṇyaka and Upaniṣad of one śākhā. The six Vedāṅgas hang as aerial roots that support the tree, and Jñāna and Mokṣa are its fruit.

source.text: The Veda is apauruṣeya: no human author composed it. The Upaniṣad calls the four Vedas the very breath of the Supreme (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4.10).

nourish.term: Water and nourishment — Śraddhā and Dharma
nourish.text: Faith, and a life lived by the Veda, keep the tree alive. They pass from generation to generation through the guru–śiṣya paramparā, shown by the teacher and students at its foot.

trunk.term: Trunk and four limbs — the Vedas
trunk.text: One Veda, divided by Vedavyāsa into the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma and Atharva Vedas: four equal limbs of a single trunk.

shakhas.text: Each Veda survives in recensions (śākhās), each preserved by its own lineage of reciters. The picture shows only some of them; more are listed below.

vedangas.text: Like a banyan's prop roots, they grow from the tree and then hold it up. Śikṣā, Kalpa, Vyākaraṇa, Nirukta, Chandas and Jyotiṣa are the disciplines for reciting, performing and understanding the Veda. They serve all four Vedas, not only the limbs they hang beside.

fruit.text: The Veda guides a life of dharma in this world (abhyudaya) and, through knowledge of Brahman, leads to liberation (niḥśreyasa).

anatomy.title: Inside one śākhā
anatomy.subtitle: Each śākhā is a complete body of texts, not just a Saṃhitā. The small twig at the centre of the tree shows the Taittirīya śākhā, growing from leaf to fruit:
anatomy.note: In the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, mantra and brāhmaṇa passages are interwoven even within the Saṃhitā, and the Upaniṣads sit inside the Āraṇyaka (prapāṭhakas 7–10). Other śākhās divide their texts differently.

others.title: Śākhās not shown in the picture
others.text: Tradition remembers far more śākhās than survive today. Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya speaks of 21 for the Ṛgveda, 101 for the Yajurveda, 1,000 paths of the Sāmaveda and 9 for the Atharvaveda. Besides those in the picture, living traditions include:
others.kanva: Śukla Yajurveda — Kāṇva, widely followed in Karnataka and Maharashtra
others.ranayaniya: Sāmaveda — Rāṇāyanīya, found mainly in Karnataka
others.krishna: Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda — Maitrāyaṇī and Kaṭha, now rare

vedaVruksha.cta: In the Knowledge Map you can choose any Veda and śākhā and walk its books — from saṃhitā to upaniṣad, with its limbs and commentaries.

about.heroSubtitle: For the Upliftment of Veda Gurukulas
about.storyPara1: Across India, Vedic Gurukulas quietly sustain one of humanity's oldest living traditions. Within their modest walls, young students rise before dawn to learn the Vedas through an unbroken oral lineage — guided by Adhyāpakas who have given their lives to mastering it.
about.storyPara2: Yet most of these Gurukulas operate with limited funding, aging infrastructure, and little public visibility — and the very teachers who sustain the tradition are often the least recognised.
about.storyPara3: Sri Shivasankalpa Vṛnda was founded to change this.
about.storyPara4: We are not a Gurukulam. We are a trust that exists so Gurukulas can thrive — identifying what they need, sharing their story with a wider community, and working alongside them to build a sustainable future for Vedic education.
about.storyShlokaTranslation: May our minds be filled with auspicious resolve.
about.storyClosing: This resolve is our foundation: to serve the Gurukulas that preserve the Vedas, and to invite others to join us in this sacred responsibility.
about.visionText: A world where every Vedic Gurukula has the resources, recognition, and community it needs to thrive — and where the Guru–Shishya Paramparā continues to illuminate generations.
about.missionText: To identify the needs of Veda Gurukulas, create public awareness about their vital role in preserving Vedic Dharma, generate financial and community support, and foster their long-term growth and sustainability.
about.objectivesSubtitle: Our work spans six core areas of support for Vedic education and heritage preservation.
about.obj0Desc: Support Vedic education in Gurukulas, fostering saṁskāra, cultural values, and the cultivation of traditional arts and skills (kalā–kauśalya).
about.obj1Desc: Foster community engagement through the organisation and participation in awareness programs, workshops, and outreach initiatives.
about.obj2Desc: Support and participate in Vedic research initiatives and help build Vedic libraries for future generations.
about.obj3Desc: Assist Gurukulas in the fulfilment of their essential needs — infrastructure, teaching materials, student nutrition, and teacher welfare.
about.obj4Desc: Honour and recognise the sacrifice of Vedic scholars and Adhyāpakas who have dedicated their lives to preserving the Gurukula tradition.
about.obj5Desc: Support the development of Gośālās and the sacred cause of cow protection, shelter, and welfare.
about.operatePara1: The Vṛnda reaches out to Gurukulas across Karnataka — beginning with Bangalore — speaking with administrators, Adhyāpakas (teachers), and Vidyārthīs (students) to identify needs and assess what assistance can be provided.
about.operatePara2: In parallel, we are building a database of Adhyāpakas and Veda Vidyārthīs — shakha, level of study, contact details — for future reference and coordination. This systematic approach ensures that our support is targeted, sustained, and responsive to real needs.
about.teamSubtitle: The individuals who guide and govern the Vṛnda's activities.
about.anugrahaPara1: The name “Sri Shivasankalpa” was bestowed upon the Vṛnda as a sacred blessing by His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri.
about.anugrahaPara2: Drawn from the Shiva Sankalpa Sukta of the Shukla Yajurveda, this name carries the prayer for a mind ever filled with auspicious resolve — and reminds us, in every endeavour, of the parampara in which we are humbly rooted.

about.govPoint0: All income and property of the Trust is applied solely towards its stated objects.

maharudra.imageAlt: Sri Adi Shankaracharya worshipping the Sphatika Linga — painting
maharudra.mapTitle: Hoysala Trust, Hosakerehalli, Bengaluru — where the Mahā Rudra Puraścaraṇa was held
maharudra.shlokaVedaTranslation: The particles of earth may be counted, the drops of rain may be counted — but even Brahma, the Creator, cannot measure the fruits of Vedādhyayana.
maharudra.introPara1: By the anugraha and blessings of His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam and His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam, the Mahārudra yāga of 16 and 17 May 2026 was completed at Hosakerehalli. Students from several Veda Gurukulas offered the Mahārudra japa, and the homa and other vaidika rites were led by the ācāryas. Devotees took part, and the Vṛnda regards the completion as entirely the fruit of the Jagadgurus’ grace. The three days had opened on the evening of 15 May.
maharudra.introPara2: In the weeks that followed, the Vṛnda visited more than ten Gurukulas, sat with the ācāryas, and began offering groceries, financial support, and what the students need. That sevā continues.
maharudra.rudraTranslation: That which melts away suffering — that is Rudra.
maharudra.rudraDesc: Rudra is the compassionate Lord who melts away the devotee's sorrow and destroys all suffering.
maharudra.shivaPuranaTranslation: All sins are destroyed for one who chants the Rudra. Through the grace of Shiva's name, one crosses the ocean of worldly existence. The root causes of worldly bondage are undoubtedly annihilated.
maharudra.shivaPuranaPara1: As described in the Shiva Purana, the ultimate goal of human birth is liberation from the cycle of birth and death and attainment of Kaivalya (Supreme Liberation). In Kali Yuga, Bhagavan has bestowed two primary paths — Karma Mārga (Path of Action) and Jñāna Mārga (Path of Knowledge). Selfless actions performed with devotion lead one towards knowledge and liberation.
maharudra.shivaPuranaPara2: The Yajur Veda, particularly the Rudrādhyāya, prescribes sacred chanting and homa that remove accumulated karmas, bestow inner purification, and lead the seeker towards Amṛtatva — immortality.
maharudra.sevaSubtitle: Devotees joined the Puraścaraṇa through these sevas.
maharudra.closingTranslation: May our minds be filled with auspicious resolve.
maharudra.closingPara: The Puraścaraṇa is complete. The sevā it was offered for — the Gurukulas — continues.
maharudra.cardSubtitle: For Loka Kalyāṇa and the support of Veda Gurukulas
maharudra.cardDescription: Completed at Hosakerehalli on 15–17 May 2026, with the blessings of the Sringeri Jagadgurus. The Mahārudra yāga of 16 and 17 May was offered by students of several Veda Gurukulas, with homa led by the ācāryas.
maharudra.day0Item0Desc: Deepa Aaradhana, Devatha Prarthana, Maha Ganapati Puja, Svasti Vachana, Deva Naandi, Panchagavya, Rakshoghna & Vastu Homa, Maha Mangalarathi
maharudra.day1Item0Desc: Kalasha Sthapane, Sahasra Modaka Maha Ganapati Homa, Mahanyasa Poorvaka Maha Rudra Japa (with Veda students), Rudrabhisheka, Maha Mangalarathi
maharudra.day2Item0Desc: Kalasha Aradhane, Kruchra Acharane, Maha Rudra Homa
maharudra.sabhaDesc: As part of the Puraścaraṇa, the Vṛnda felicitated Vaidika scholars at a sabhā presided over by Śrī Krishnamurthy Ghanapāṭhī (Daśagranthī), a Vaidika scholar of rare standing. The full sabhā, including his address in Kannada, is recorded here.
maharudra.albumSubtitle: Moments from Mahā Rudra Puraścaraṇa, 15–17 May 2026.
maharudra.nivedanaIntro: After the Puraścaraṇa, the Vṛnda submitted this nivedana at the lotus feet of the Jagadgurus.
maharudra.nivedanaBody:
Śrī Gurubhyo Namaḥ.
Śrī Śāradāmbāyai Namaḥ.

Offering praṇāmas with devotion at the divine lotus feet of Paramapūjya Śrīmaj Jagadguru Śrī Śrī Bhāratī Tīrtha Mahāsannidhānam, and of Paramapūjya Śrīmaj Jagadguru Śrī Śrī Vidhuśekhara Bhāratī Mahāsannidhānam, born of those sacred lotus feet.

We, the Śivasankalpa Vṛnda of Bengaluru, submit this humble nivedana.

By your divine anugraha and blessings, the Mahārudra yāga held on 16 and 17 May was completed with great success. We report this with joy at your lotus feet. Students of various Veda Gurukulas offered the Mahārudra japa, and homa and other vaidika rites were conducted under the lead of the Gurukulas’ ācāryas. With the active participation of devotees, the whole programme was fulfilled in a meaningful way and with spiritual splendour.

We regard this success entirely as the fruit of your gracious glance.

During your vijaya yātrā in Tumakuru we had offered this resolve of dharma-sevā in your presence and sought your blessings. Out of your compassion you bestowed on our group the divine name “Śivasankalpa Vṛnda.” From that day, by the strength of your blessings, this sevā has met with a warm response from society, and many openings have continued to come for Gurukula sevā, the protection of the Veda, and dharmic work.

After the Mahārudra yāga we were blessed to visit more than ten Gurukulas. We sat with the ācāryas and those who look after the pāṭhaśālas, came to know their needs and difficulties, and the resolve to take part in Gurukula sevā to the extent of our strength grew firmer.

By your blessings and the cooperation of good people, Śivasankalpa Vṛnda today serves as a small bridge between society and the Gurukulas. We have taken up the work of reaching them with groceries, financial support, and help for the students’ education and daily needs. Many who love dharma, and many donors, have joined this puṇya-kārya.

From the day you granted the name “Śivasankalpa Vṛnda,” this sevā has received extraordinary support. In truth, behind all of this there is no personal capacity of ours. All of it is the fruit of your divine saṅkalpa. That saṅkalpa is the strength that leads us; we are only the occasion through which it takes form.

We pray that your kṛpā, guidance, and anugraha may always rest on us, so that this work — the uplift of the Gurukulas, the protection of the Veda, and the sevā of Sanātana Dharma — may grow yet wider.

We offer countless praṇāmas at your divine lotus feet.

In humility,
Śivasankalpa Vṛnda
Bengaluru

Śrī Gurubhyo Namaḥ.
Śrī Śāradāmbāyai Namaḥ.

enrol.shlokaTranslation: Lead us from darkness into Light.
enrol.title: Let Your Child Grow in the Light of the Vedas
enrol.para1: In a world of constant distraction, the Gurukula offers something timeless — a life rooted in dharma, humility, discipline, devotion, and sacred learning.
enrol.para2: Under the care of revered Adhyāpakas, children are nurtured not only in Veda, but in character, conduct, reverence, and inner strength.
enrol.closing: The ancient Guru–Śiṣya Paramparā lives on. May the next generation carry its light forward.
enrol.cta: Choose a Gurukula for Your Child
enrol.admissionsNote: Admissions are open in participating Gurukulas

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.subtitle: Common questions about the trust, our work, and how you can participate.
faqs.a0: Sri Shivasankalpa Trust is a charitable trust dedicated to supporting Vedic education in Gurukulas, fostering saṁskāra and cultural values, and sustaining the timeless Guru–Shishya Parampara. The name "Sri Shivasankalpa" was given as a blessing by the Jagadguru of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham.
faqs.a1: The word comes from the Shiva Sankalpa Sukta of the Shukla Yajurveda — "तन्मे मनः शिवसङ्कल्पमस्तु" (Tan me manaḥ śivasaṅkalpamastu) — a prayer that means "May my mind be filled with auspicious resolve." It reflects our aspiration that every action we take is guided by noble, dharmic intention.
faqs.a2: Donations support three primary causes: (1) Gurukula Abhivruddhi — direct support to Vedic Gurukulas for infrastructure, teaching materials, and student welfare; (2) Go-Samrakshanam — supporting Gośālās and cow welfare; (3) Event Seva — funding sacred events like the Maharudra Purascharana that benefit the broader community.
faqs.q3: How can I participate in trust activities?
faqs.a3: You can take part through tanu (physical service), mana (devotion and spreading awareness), and dhana (financial contributions). The Mahā Rudra Puraścaraṇa is complete; ongoing seva is with the Gurukulas. Write to us if you would like to help.
faqs.a4: We are in the process of obtaining 80G certification. Once approved, donations will be eligible for tax benefits under Section 80G of the Income Tax Act. We will update this page when the certification is in place.
faqs.q5: Which Gurukulas does the trust support?
faqs.a5: The Vṛnda is engaged with seventeen Gurukulas and pāṭhaśālas. In Bengaluru: Sri Shruti Parampara Gurukulam (JP Nagar), Namma Sampradaya Gurukulam (Sarjapura), Mallige Pāṭhaśālā (Malleswaram), Sri Mallikarjuna Veda Vidyā Gurukula — also called Jyothi Pāṭhaśālā — (Shankarapura, near Basavanagudi), Sacchidananda Advaitāśrama (Rajajinagar), Gowtama Veda Pāṭhaśālā (Sapthagiri Layout), Bharati Tīrtha Veda Pāṭhaśālā at the Sringeri Shankara Mutt (Shankarapura), Vedanāda Gurukula (Turahalli), and Seva Niketana (Basavanagudi). Also Shankara Gurukulam (Ungra, Huliyurdurga), Sri Chidambarāśrama (Gubbi, Tumakuru), and Sri Ramana Maharṣi Brahma Vidyāśrama (Madagondapalli, Hosur). In the Sirsi region: Uma Madhukeshwara Veda Vidyā Gurukula (Banavasi), Śrauta Vijñāna Gurukulam (Nadagodu), and Sri Veda Prakāśa Gurukula (Danandi); Śrīdhara Sāṅga Veda Vidyā Gurukula (Varadahalli, Sagara); and Koodali Shankara Mutt (Shivamogga). Each one is listed on the Gurukulas page.
faqs.a6: We welcome volunteers for event coordination, Gurukula visits, documentation, and outreach. Please write to us at info@shivasankalpa.org with a brief note about how you would like to contribute.
faqs.q7: What is the trust's connection to Sringeri?
faqs.a7: Sri Shivasankalpa Vrunda was blessed and named by the Jagadguru of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri. The trust considers the blessings and guidance of the Sringeri Jagadgurus as paramount and operates in alignment with the Advaita Vedanta tradition of Adi Shankaracharya.

resources.title: Vedic Knowledge Map
resources.subtitle: Read the Veda the way it is learned — one śākhā at a time, from saṃhitā to upaniṣad, with the limbs and commentaries that belong to it.
resources.intro: The Veda is not a single book. Each Veda is carried by its śākhās (recensions), and each śākhā has its own set of books: a saṃhitā of mantras, a brāhmaṇa that explains the rites, an āraṇyaka and an upaniṣad, and the sūtras that put them into practice. Bhāṣyas are the voices of the ācāryas who explained these texts; you will find them beside the book they explain, not as another layer of the Veda.
resources.how1Body: Four doors — the Yajurveda opens into its Śukla and Kṛṣṇa halves.
resources.how2Body: Each śākhā is one living line of recitation with its own books.
resources.how3Body: A single path from saṃhitā to upaniṣad, then its limbs. Open any book for what it is and where to hear or read it.
resources.doorsSubtitle: Open a door, then choose the śākhā you want to walk.
resources.shelfTitle: The six limbs of the Veda
resources.shelfSubtitle: Śikṣā and Kalpa live on each śākhā’s path. Vyākaraṇa, Nirukta, Chandas and Jyotiṣa serve every Veda and sit on a shared shelf.
resources.shelfShlokaTranslation: Chandas is the feet of the Veda, Kalpa its hands, Jyotiṣa its eyes, Nirukta its ears, Śikṣā its nose, and Vyākaraṇa its mouth.
resources.librariesSubtitle: Every link on this map was opened and checked. We point to a few good sources per book rather than every copy on the internet.
resources.scopeNote: This first edition covers the Veda and its Upaniṣads. Darśana, Itihāsa and Purāṇa will follow.
